moduleTitle: Module 10: How to Use the App
title: 10.4 Journal, Profile Settings, Talent, and Supporting Workflows
summary: Trading is not only about clicking `Buy` or `Sell`.
bodyHtml:
10.4 Journal, Profile Settings, Talent, and Supporting Workflows

Why This Matters

Trading is not only about clicking Buy or Sell.

A complete beginner also needs to know:

  • where to review thoughts and mistakes
  • where to secure the account
  • where to manage devices and verification
  • where supporting screens like Talent fit into the platform

This lesson covers those routes using the exact wording currently shown inside the app.

What You Should Understand After This Lesson

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

  • create and edit entries in Trading Journal;
  • move through every section chip in Profile Settings;
  • recognize the Identity Verification and Devices & Activity workflows;
  • understand what Talent is and which labels appear there.

Trading Journal

The journal route is /journal.

When you open it, the page title is Trading Journal and the subtitle is:

Track your thoughts, emotions, and lessons

The main create button is:

  • New Entry

When you open the entry dialog, you see:

  • New Journal Entry
  • Your thoughts
  • Link to Trade(s) (Optional)
  • Current Mood
  • Tags
  • Cancel
  • Save Entry

The edit version uses:

  • Edit Journal Entry
  • Update Entry

Useful search and filter labels include:

  • Search entries...
  • All Moods

If there are no entries yet, you can see:

  • No journal entries yet
  • Create Your First Entry

If you are not signed in, the page can show:

  • Please log in to view your trading journal.
  • Go to Login

Journal Moods and Tags

The Current Mood menu includes these exact mood labels:

  • Confident
  • Calm
  • Anxious
  • Frustrated
  • Fearful
  • Greedy
  • Neutral

The common tag set includes labels such as:

  • Breakout
  • Trend following
  • Reversal
  • Scalp
  • Swing
  • News-driven
  • Technical
  • Fundamental
  • Lesson learned
  • Mistake
  • Over trading
  • Profitable
  • Loss

You can also type a custom tag using Add custom tag... and the Add button.

Profile Settings

The profile route is /profile.

The page title is Profile Settings, and the subtitle says:

Manage your account information and security

The section chips across the page are:

  • My Profile
  • Security & Login
  • Identity Verification
  • Devices & Activity
  • Preferences

Those five chips are the main beginner map for the whole settings page.

My Profile

Inside My Profile, the main card heading is Account Information.

Important field labels are:

  • Email
  • Username
  • Full Name
  • Phone Number

The save button is:

  • Save Changes

The page also tells you:

  • Email cannot be changed

Security & Login

Inside Security & Login, a beginner will see several important cards.

Account Security

This area includes:

  • Account Security
  • Account Status
  • Member Since
  • Two-Factor Authentication
  • Enable 2FA
  • Disable

Trusted Devices

This card is titled:

  • Trusted Devices

It can also show:

  • Revoke All
  • No trusted devices

Each stored device has a red icon button for one-device removal.

Change Password

The password card uses:

  • Change Password
  • Current Password
  • New Password
  • Confirm New Password

The page also has eye buttons to show or hide the password text.

Account Deactivation & Deletion

This section includes:

  • Deactivate Account
  • Delete Account

Its confirmation dialog uses:

  • Reason
  • Additional details (optional)
  • Password
  • Type DELETE to confirm
  • Type DEACTIVATE to confirm

Identity Verification

Inside Identity Verification, the section heading is:

  • Verification & Security

The verified cards inside it are:

  • Email Verification
  • Phone Verification
  • KYC Verification
  • Payout Settings

Important visible actions can include:

  • Send Verification Email
  • Send Code
  • Verify
  • Start KYC Process
  • Request Payout

Status wording can include:

  • Verified
  • Pending
  • Not Verified
  • Available for selected traders only
  • Available after KYC approval

Devices & Activity

This section is where beginners manage sessions and recent access.

Important headings and actions include:

  • Active Sessions
  • Terminate All Others
  • Current
  • Recent Login Activity

Inside login activity, status labels can include:

  • Successful login
  • Failed login attempt
  • Success
  • Failed

If there is nothing to show, the page can display:

  • No active sessions
  • No login history available

Preferences

The Preferences section contains three main cards:

  • Regional Preferences
  • Notification Preferences
  • Trading Preferences

Regional Preferences

Important labels include:

  • Timezone
  • Language
  • Country / Region
  • Save Preferences

You may also see:

  • Timezone editing is disabled by an administrator.
  • Country is locked to your signup jurisdiction.

Notification Preferences

The switch labels are:

  • Trade Executed
  • Margin Warning
  • Stop Loss / Take Profit Hit
  • Daily Summary
  • Promotions & Updates

Trading Preferences

This card explains account-level settings such as leverage and trade limits, and it currently shows:

  • Leverage
  • Max Trades

Talent

The dashboard tab labeled Leaderboard on desktop opens a page titled Talent.

The visible sub-tabs can include:

  • Leaderboard
  • My Resume
  • Compete
  • Community

Inside the main leaderboard view, beginners should recognize:

  • Top Traders
  • My Rank
  • the column labels Rank, Trader, P/L, and Win Rate

Notifications as a Supporting Workflow

The header bell is also part of the normal user experience.

Its panel title is:

  • Notifications

Inside the panel, the main text action is:

  • Mark all

This belongs in the public guide because it is trader-facing and visible in normal use.
learningOutcomes: use the dedicated `Trading Journal` route and its create/edit tools confidently;
navigate every `Profile Settings` section chip and understand the key cards and action labels inside each;
recognize the `Talent` screen and its optional sub-tabs;
understand the difference between trader-facing workflows and admin-only controls that must stay out of the public guide.
